- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model tends to overreact to recent spikes — dampen forecast peaks by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment rose sharply 3–5 days prior, forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- Avoid long-term horizon overconfidence — if 30-day forecast is >15% above 18-day history, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Price corrections after spikes: if forecast peaks >10% above prior high, reduce by 5–10% to reflect likely mean reversion.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment >0.7 but price forecast <10% above recent high, increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.
